- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing the true price’s sustained upward trend or mean-reversion pattern.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., 75→79) are common, leading to overcorrection downward.
- Model underestimates the true mean price level in the later half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting a lag in capturing long-term momentum.
- Forecasts show strong bias toward higher values, particularly when historical prices are rising; model fails to adjust downward when momentum weakens.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds high forecasts even when true prices begin to decline, suggesting lack of dynamic adjustment.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high, especially in the first 10 days, then gradually converge but still overestimate by 1–3% on average.
- Model reacts too slowly to sudden price drops or spikes — often misses the true turning point by 1–3 days.
